title: Turn board minutes into an action tracker
context: Oliver Grant has drafted the 15 October 2026 board minutes and must chase action owners before the January board.
goal: Use Copilot to extract every action, owner and due date from the minutes and draft a chaser email to owners.
task_steps: Open Board Minutes — 15 October 2026 in Word
Ask Copilot to summarise the decisions and list all actions with owners and due dates
Check the list against the action log section of the minutes
In Outlook, ask Copilot to draft a short chaser email to the owners of open actions
Edit the tone and save it as a draft
sample_prompts: Summarise the decisions taken in this board meeting in five bullet points.
List every action in these minutes as a table with action reference, owner, due date and status.
Draft an email to the owners of the open actions from /Board Minutes — 15 October 2026 reminding them of their due dates. Keep it under 150 words.
success_criteria: All seven actions (A-2610-01 to A-2610-07) captured with correct owners and dates
The three board resolutions (Copilot rollout, coach recruitment, risk appetite) identified
Email names the next board date (21 January 2027) and shares no confidential financial detail beyond what owners need
Learner checks Copilot output against the source rather than copying it blindly
trainer_notes: Point out the minutes are Draft (v0.3) and Confidential — a good moment to discuss sensitivity labels and who should receive what.

title: Build a Policy Finder agent
context: Amy Collins answers the same policy questions all day — gifts, whistleblowing, who owns which policy and when it is due for review.
goal: Create a SharePoint agent grounded on the Hub's Company Policies library that answers staff policy questions with citations and points to the policy owner.
task_steps: Open Delcorn Hub > Company Policies and create an agent from the library
Test with the sample prompts and check each answer against the cited policy
Ask a question the library cannot answer (e.g. annual leave carry-over) and confirm the agent refers you to the owner in the Policy Index rather than guessing
Share the agent with a colleague for feedback
sample_prompts: A client has offered me tickets to a match worth about £300. Can I accept?
How can I report a concern anonymously?
Who owns the AI Acceptable Use Policy and when is it next reviewed?
Which policies are overdue for review?
What does the Code of Conduct say about connecting with learners on social media?
success_criteria: Gift answer cites the £50 registration and £250 CFO approval thresholds
Whistleblowing answer gives the Safeline Speak Up number and the NED champion
Answers cite the source document and the policy owner
Agent declines to give legal advice and does not invent policies that are not in the library
Overdue policies identified correctly from the Policy Index
agent_instructions: You are Delcorn's Policy Finder. Answer questions from Delcorn staff using only the documents in the Company Policies library on the Delcorn Hub. Always: (1) give a short, plain-English answer in UK English; (2) quote the specific threshold, timescale or contact from the policy; (3) cite the policy name and version; (4) name the policy owner from the Policy Index so the person knows who to ask. If the answer is not in the library, say so and point to the owner listed in the Policy Index — never guess. Do not give legal advice. For safeguarding concerns about a learner, tell the user to contact the Designated Safeguarding Lead the same working day.
trainer_notes: Several policies in the index live on other sites — discuss widening the knowledge sources versus keeping the agent narrowly scoped.

title: CEO briefing for the Meridian trading update
context: Helena Marsh has a call with Meridian's Group COO and wants a one-page briefing that joins up the October board pack, the latest funding data and the pipeline.
goal: Produce a one-page, board-ready briefing combining the board pack, the Q1 email thread and live data, with every figure traceable to a source.
task_steps: Ask Copilot to summarise the October board pack's key messages and decisions
Ground on the Meridian Q1 trading update email thread to capture what the group asked for
Use the monthly_funding and opportunities data (Excel or Power BI) to check FY2026/27 YTD funding and the weighted pipeline
Ask Copilot to draft a one-page briefing under Meridian's five headings
Add a 'questions Richard may ask' section and verify every number against the sources
sample_prompts: Using /Board Pack — October 2026 and the email 'Q1 FY2026/27 trading update for Meridian group board', draft a one-page briefing for my call with Richard Alder.
What are the top three corporate risks and has anything changed since the board?
From the monthly funding data, how much apprenticeship funding have we earned in Aug–Oct 2026, by academy?
List five tough questions Meridian might ask about the Level 7 impact, with suggested answers.
success_criteria: YTD funding, weighted pipeline and top risk match the data
Briefing follows Meridian's five-point format and fits on one page
Level 7 impact (c.£0.9m over two years) and mitigation plan included
Copilot go-live dates and conditions stated correctly
Sources cited for every figure; no learner personal data included
agent_instructions: You are the CEO's briefing assistant. Produce concise, board-ready briefings for Helena Marsh in UK English. Lead with what it means for learners and the business, keep to one page, and cite the source document or dataset for every number. Flag any figure that differs between sources rather than silently choosing one. Treat board material as Confidential and never include personal data about learners or staff.
trainer_notes: Encourage learners to notice that the board pack KPI says 'latest ILR' while the email quotes Aug–Oct — a useful discussion on data currency.
